data.prompt:
You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajc-p1
Title: AJC prover p1: claim and close the 1st-most important representability item
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
References: roadmap=AJC.jacobian,AJC.picrep,AJC.picrep.tensor; inbox=I-0838

You are prover lane `ajc-p1` on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge. This round the objective is deliberately FREE: nobody has told you which declaration to prove. Your objective is to identify the MOST important open item standing between this project and Picard/Pic^0 representability, claim it publicly, and discharge it.

READ FIRST: protection item `I-0838`. It is the claim protocol for this round's ten parallel lanes and it is not optional — steps 2 through 5 (check ownership, claim with `roadmap set --owner ajc-p1`, announce, release on exit) are what stop four lanes proving the same lemma. Also read `I-0491` and `I-0492`, the two binding human decisions, before touching the seam.

YOUR RANK. You take the MOST important item. Rank is a tie-break so four lanes do not converge on one target, not a fence: if your item turns out to be blocked on another lane's, say so in the inbox and swap. On a contested item you first refusal on any contested item.

YOUR PEERS this round are ajc-p1, ajc-p2, ajc-p3, ajc-p4 plus the reviewer `review-ajc`. The reviewer is auditing route and organisation and will be correcting the board in its first hour — read its inbox items before you fix your target, and re-read them if you are about to start something large. It may direct-message you a proposal; weigh it against what you hold, and take it if it is genuinely worth more. You may propose work to the other lanes the same way (`inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane>`), naming declaration, file, and why it beats what they hold.

HOW TO CHOOSE, since this is the part I am delegating to you. "Most important" means: measured against the project's representability headline, what does discharging this buy? A leaf that unblocks three others beats a leaf that is merely nearest. A leaf whose stated prerequisite turns out to already exist in the file beats both — earlier sessions' costings in this workspace have been wrong in that direction more than once, so read the actual Lean hypothesis, not the prose about it. Use `horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier` for the ranked view, `horizon roadmap list --focus AJC.picrep / AJC.jacobian` for the board, and `horizon search` (which spans both projects AND mathlib) before you prove anything — the premise you need is often already next door under a name you would not have grepped.

THE BAR, and it is higher than usual this round. An audit on 2026-07-29 sampled 101 representability claims across both projects and refuted 99: 67 were sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 proved something adjacent to what they claimed, 3 did not exist. So:
- Sorry-free is necessary, not sufficient. Before you report a gate closed, exhibit a witness for EVERY antecedent, or state plainly which antecedent remains undischarged. "The implication is proved" and "the conclusion holds for some curve" are different claims and I want to know which you have.
- Never introduce a class, structure field, or side condition whose statement does not mention the object it is about. The cautionary case is `HasDivFunctor`: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, the curve did not occur, and the blueprint advertised it as the existence of the divisor functor with `\leanok`. It survived because nobody read the statement.
- Never discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed. `choose_spec.1` of your own binder is `P → P`.
- A green build is not evidence of non-vacuity, and `lean_multi_attempt` reports every snippet as closing the goal when the file's imports are stale. Check imports before believing a probe.
- Do not restate an obligation more weakly to make a count go down. If you cannot close it, leave it open and say why.

ONE SHARED LEDGER, ten writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once — write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`. Commit at every coherent point; an interrupted lane loses only what was uncommitted. Follow the `lean-check` LSP loop for edits and keep `lake build` for the session boundary — nine other lanes want the build lock too.

WHERE THIS PROJECT ACTUALLY STANDS, so you do not rediscover it. The entire Jacobian tower rests on ONE bare `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability` at `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:347`. Its unique consumer chain runs through `instHasPicSchemeEt` (an unconditional producer that is a projection of that sorry) to the headline. The legacy `HasPicScheme` class has NO instance, so the ~45 declarations taking `[HasPicScheme C]` currently prove nothing about any curve. `instPicSharpRepresentable` and `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` are `choose_spec` projections of their own hypothesis. `smoothProperQuotient` proves `P.IsRepresentable → P.IsRepresentable` with all four Kleiman hypotheses unused and zero call sites. `HasDivFunctor` is vacuous as described above.

The line-347 docstring says discharging it needs Kleiman §4 — the Abel-map slice `Div^d → Pic^d` as a smooth proper equivalence relation with scheme quotient, plus `Div` representability via Quot — while the board marks BOTH `AJC.picrep.quot` and `AJC.picrep.serre` `rejected`. That contradiction is the reviewer's first assignment; if it resolves before you fix your target, use its answer.

Board caveat: `AJC.picrep` is marked `done` and its advertised deliverable `instHasPicScheme` exists in no `.lean` file — deleted 2026-07-28 under `I-0491`, not discharged. Do not read `done` on that subtree as truth until the reviewer has corrected it. Open non-done items you might weigh: `AJC.picrep.tensor` (pullback-tensor and fibre base change), `AJC.rr.extuniform` (extension-uniform H1 vanishing, one threshold serving every fibre), `AJC.fbc.cosimplicial.twisted` (the twisted Čech nerve naturality square that separates this project from Stacks 02KH), `AJC.pic0av.tangent` / `.structure` / `.identity`, `AJC.albanese.symmetric` / `.universal`. Body-position sorries live in `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` (6), `Jacobian.lean` (4), `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` (3), `Picard/SerreFiniteness.lean` (2), `Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean` (2), `Picard/Pic0Et.lean` (2), `Picard/IdentityComponent.lean` (2), `Picard/QuotRepresentability.lean` (1), `FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (1), `Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean` (1).

A real option, and I want you to consider it seriously rather than defaulting to a leaf: the sibling project Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild has a genuinely sorry-free representability engine (`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, `Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) whose inputs are chart data rather than Quot. `horizon search` spans both projects. If AJC's route is blocked on Quot and the sibling's is not, the highest-value thing a lane can do here may be to import or transcribe that route rather than push on Kleiman §4. Price it before you commit to it — a cross-project object-level match can be true and still irrelevant if the carrier the statement binds differs.

WHAT I WANT AT THE END. Your report should answer three things without me having to ask: which item you claimed and why it was the most important one, what its state is now (closed sorry-free with all antecedents witnessed / closed as an implication with named antecedents still open / advanced with the remaining obligation stated / blocked, with the blocker), and what you learned that changes another lane's plan. If you found a costing wrong, a vacuity, or a route problem, that goes in the inbox as an `issue` at the site that made the claim — not only in your report, which nobody downstream reads.

If your first-choice item collapses on inspection — the prerequisite already exists, or the statement turns out vacuous, or another lane got there first — that is a finding, not a wasted session. Record it, release the claim, and take the next item. Do not sit on a claimed item you are not working.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

420	so transporting it to `Pic0SchemeEt` needs the comparison of the two Picard schemes,
421	which is available only under a section. That transport is the honest remaining cost of
422	the étale formulation at this leaf, and it is why this is a separate statement rather
423	than a corollary. -/
424	theorem smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
425	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
426	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
427	  sorry
428	
429	/-- **Leaf B's dimension count, at the headline and against the landed development.**
430	
431	The number `genus C` in leaf B is not an arbitrary index: it is the dimension of the
432	Zariski tangent space of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` at the identity, and *that* identity is landed
433	mathematics (`Scheme.Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne`, the Kleiman §5
434	Thm 5.11 chain through the truncated-exponential splitting and the Mayer–Vietoris
435	comparison). Since `genus C` is by definition `dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, the two sides match
436	with no transport, exactly as leaf C's `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed` matches
437	`Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property`.
438	
439	Stating it here fixes what leaf B still owes, which is easy to misjudge from the leaf
440	alone. It is *not* the dimension count. It is the two steps that turn a tangent-space
441	dimension into a relative dimension:
442	
443	1. `Scheme.Pic0.smooth` — bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` over `k`, itself `sorry`-bodied
444	   upstream, so leaf B presupposes an obligation rather than reducing one. That obligation
445	   is smaller than it looks, and worth stating here because it changes what a reader should
446	   expect to have to build: its *entire* remaining content is
447	   `GeometricallyReduced (Pic⁰_{C/k}).hom`. Mathlib's public `smooth_of_grpObj` takes
448	   `[LocallyOfFiniteType f]`, `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` and `[GeometricallyReduced f]` and
449	   returns `Smooth f` over an arbitrary field, so the translation argument that propagates
450	   smoothness from the identity is already done there; the first two inputs are landed
451	   (`Pic0.locallyOfFiniteType`, `Pic0.grpObj`) and elaborate at these hypotheses verbatim,
452	   while `GeometricallyReduced` does not synthesize and its only producer in the tree is
453	   `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular. So `Pic0.smooth` is Cartier's
454	   theorem in characteristic zero and a genuine characteristic-`p` statement otherwise —
455	   not a translation argument. "Entire remaining content" is meant strictly, and it is
456	   measured rather than estimated: the conclusion of `Pic0.smooth`, proved at that
457	   theorem's binders verbatim with `GeometricallyReduced` as the sole added hypothesis, is
458	   **axiom-clean** — `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, where `Pic0.smooth` itself
459	   reports `sorryAx`. So supplying geometric reducedness discharges it outright, with no
460	   residual leak elsewhere in the assembly;
461	2. the passage from "smooth, with `dim_{κ(e)} T_e = n`" to
462	   `SmoothOfRelativeDimension n`. Mathlib defines the latter by local standard-smooth
463	   presentations, not by a tangent-space dimension. There *is* a bridge, but it is at the
464	   algebra level and it goes through a different invariant:
465	   `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.iff_of_isStandardSmooth` characterises
466	   relative dimension `n` as `Module.rank S Ω[S⁄R] = n`, the rank of the module of Kähler
467	   differentials. So the missing mathematics is (i) the identification of that rank with
468	   the tangent-space dimension at the identity — over a field these are dual to one
469	   another, but the statement has to be made and the duality is where a rank/`finrank`
470	   mismatch would bite — and (ii) the passage from an affine-local statement about
471	   presentations to the scheme-level class, which quantifies over an affine cover of
472	   `Pic⁰_{C/k}` rather than over a single point.
473	
474	   This is worth stating precisely rather than as "no bridge exists", which an earlier
475	   version of this docstring claimed: the leaf's cost is a translation between two
476	   invariants of smoothness, not the construction of one from nothing.
477	
478	Like `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`, this is a faithful record of a distance rather
479	than a discharge: its axioms carry `sorryAx`, because the dimension chain it invokes
480	still rests on `Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_finrank_h1Cok`. -/
481	theorem finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
482	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
483	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
484	    [Scheme.HasPicScheme C] [Scheme.PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
485	    Module.finrank
486	        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField
487	          ((Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
488	            ((Scheme.Pic0.identitySection C).base default)))
489	        (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace
490	          ((Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
491	            ((Scheme.Pic0.identitySection C).base default)))
492	      = genus C :=
493	  Scheme.Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne C
494	
495	/-- **Leaf C: the Albanese universal property, over an arbitrary field and every point.**
496	
497	`Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` proves exactly this statement, but under two
498	restrictions the witness cannot accept: the base field is algebraically closed, and the
499	genus is positive. The witness needs the property over the ambient field `k` and for
500	*every* choice of `k`-rational marked point `P`, including `genus C = 0` (where
501	`Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k` and the content is the classical rigidity statement that every
502	pointed morphism from a genus-`0` curve to an abelian variety is constant).
503	
504	Descending the algebraically-closed case to `k` is the Galois-descent step of the
505	campaign's cluster `G`; the genus-`0` case is Mumford §4 rigidity.
506	
507	`isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed` below is the same statement in the case the landed
508	proof covers, and it is a theorem rather than a leaf: it shows the *only* content this
509	leaf adds over the landed `Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property`, beyond the two
510	restrictions named above, is the basepoint condition. -/
511	theorem isAlbanese_pic0 (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
512	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
513	    [Scheme.HasPicScheme C] [Scheme.PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
514	    (grp : GrpObj (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C)) (pr : IsProper (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
515	    (sm : Smooth (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
516	    (gi : GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
517	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
518	    @IsAlbanese k _ C P (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C) grp pr sm gi :=
519	  sorry
520	
521	/-- **Leaf C, étale formulation: the Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`.**
522	
523	The same statement as `isAlbanese_pic0`, for the identity component of the scheme
524	representing the étale-sheafified functor — over an arbitrary base field, for every
525	`k`-rational marked point, and with **no hypothesis on `C(k)`**.
526	
527	Its content over the landed `Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` is the three
528	pieces recorded on `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`: arbitrary base field in place of
529	algebraically closed (the Galois-descent step of cluster `G`), `genus C = 0` as well as
530	positive genus (Mumford §4 rigidity), and the basepoint condition `P ≫ ι_P = η`. To those
531	the étale formulation adds the same transport `isAlbanese_pic0` does not need: the landed
532	Abel–Jacobi morphism `Pic0.abelJacobi` is constructed for `Pic0Scheme`, and carrying it
533	to `Pic0SchemeEt` is part of this leaf.
534	
535	Note that the marked point `P` appears here as an argument, not as a hypothesis on `C`:
536	`IsAlbanese` is a statement *about* a pointing, and `JacobianWitness.isAlbaneseFor`
537	quantifies over all of them. That is exactly why the headline needs no rational point —
538	the witness scheme `J` is intrinsic to `C`, and only the universal morphism depends on a
539	choice of `P`, in the same way `Challenge.lean` binds a point only in
540	`AbelJacobi.Jacobian.ofCurve`. -/
541	theorem isAlbanese_pic0Et (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
542	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
543	    (grp : GrpObj (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C)) (pr : IsProper (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C).hom)
544	    (sm : Smooth (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C).hom)
545	    (gi : GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C).hom)
546	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
547	    @IsAlbanese k _ C P (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C) grp pr sm gi :=
548	  sorry
549	
550	/-- **Leaf C in the case the landed proof covers**, over an algebraically closed field and
551	in positive genus, with the basepoint condition as an explicit hypothesis.
552	
553	This is a theorem, and it is the honest measure of the distance between
554	`isAlbanese_pic0` and the Albanese development. The factorisation clause of `IsAlbanese`
555	-- the whole universal property -- is `Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` applied
556	directly, with no transport: `Pic0.jacobianScheme C` is `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C`, so the
557	statements match on the nose. What `isAlbanese_pic0` adds is therefore three pieces of

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
8	
9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
27	hypothesis.
28	
29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
30	supplied:
31	
32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
40	
41	## The site
42	
43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
52	hypothesis.
53	
54	## Main definitions
55	
56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
57	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
58	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
59	  relative Picard presheaf.
60	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
61	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
62	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
63	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
64	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
65	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
66	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
67	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
68	  must match.
69	
70	## References
71	
72	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
73	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
74	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
75	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
76	-/
77	
78	set_option autoImplicit false
79	
80	universe u
81	
82	open CategoryTheory
83	
84	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
85	
86	namespace Scheme
87	
88	/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/
89	
90	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
91	
92	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
93	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
94	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
95	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
96	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
97	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).
98	
99	This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
100	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
101	produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
102	`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
103	want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
104	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
105	noncomputable abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
106	    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
107	  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
108	
109	/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
110	of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
111	`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
112	monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
113	sieve on the underlying scheme.
114	
115	Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
116	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
117	étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
118	theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
119	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
120	  intro T S hS
121	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
122	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS
123	
124	namespace PicSharp
125	
126	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
127	
128	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
129	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
130	
131	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
132	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
133	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
134	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
135	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
136	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.
137	
138	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
139	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
140	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
141	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
142	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
143	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
144	
145	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
146	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
147	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
148	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
149	noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
150	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
151	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
152	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
153	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
154	
155	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
156	
157	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
158	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
159	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
160	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
161	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
162	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
163	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
164	
165	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
166	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
167	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
168	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
169	  (etaleSheaf C).property
170	
171	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
172	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
173	
174	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
175	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
176	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
177	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
178	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
179	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
180	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
181	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
182	
183	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
184	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
185	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
186	
187	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
188	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
189	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
190	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
191	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
193	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
194	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
195	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
196	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
197	
198	end PicSharp

201	
202	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
203	
204	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
205	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
206	forgotten,
207	
208	```
209	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
210	```
211	
212	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
213	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
214	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
215	`picSharp`.
216	
217	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
218	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
219	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
220	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
221	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
222	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
223	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
224	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
225	
226	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
227	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
228	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
229	
230	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
231	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
232	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
233	the name is not available here). -/
234	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
235	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
236	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
237	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
238	  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
239	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
240	
241	/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**
242	
243	The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
244	because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
245	sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
246	functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
247	the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
248	unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
249	theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
250	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
251	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
252	    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) := by
253	  have h := ((CategoryTheory.sheafCompose (etaleTopologyOver k)
254	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})).obj (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C)).property
255	  rw [CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type] at h
256	  exact h

258	end PicScheme

Authors: Calle Sönne, Joël Riou, Ravi Vakil

module

public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Representable
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.BigZariski
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.OpenImmersion
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.GluingOneHypercover
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyBijective
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Products
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Iso

/-!
# Representability of schemes is a local property

In this file we prove that a sheaf of types `F` on `Sch` is representable if it is
locally representable.

## Main result
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.isRepresentable`:
  Suppose
  * F is a `Type u`-valued sheaf on `Sch` with respect to the Zariski topology
  * X : ι → Sch is a family of schemes
  * f : Π i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F is a family of relatively representable open immersions
  * f is jointly surjective

  Then `F` is representable.

## References
* https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01JJ

-/

@[expose] public section

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open CategoryTheory Category Limits Opposite

universe u

namespace Scheme

/-
Consider the following setup:
* F is `Type u`-valued a sheaf on `Sch` with respect to the Zariski topology
* X : ι → Sch is a family of schemes
* f : Π i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F is a family of relatively representable open immersions

Later, we will also assume:
* The family f is locally surjective with respect to the Zariski topology
-/
variable (F : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u))
  {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
  (f : (i : ι) → yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ F.1) (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))

namespace LocalRepresentability

variable {F f} (i j k : ι)

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
open Functor.relativelyRepresentable in
/-- We get a family of gluing data by taking `U i = X i` and `V i j = (hf i).rep.pullback (f j)`. -/
@[simps]
noncomputable def glueData : GlueData where
  J := ι
  U := X
  V := fun (i, j) ↦ (hf i).rep.pullback (f j)
  f i j := (hf i).rep.fst' (f j)
  f_mono i j :=
    have := (hf j).property _ _ _ ((hf i).1.isPullback' (f j)).flip
    IsOpenImmersion.mono _
  f_id i := IsOpenImmersion.isIso_fst'_self IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms (hf i)
  t i j := (hf i).rep.symmetry (hf j).rep
  t_id i := by apply (hf i).rep.hom_ext' <;>
    simp [IsOpenImmersion.fst'_self_eq_snd IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms (hf i)]
  t' i j k := lift₃ _ _ _ (pullback₃.p₂ _ _ _) (pullback₃.p₃ _ _ _) (pullback₃.p₁ _ _ _)
    (by simp) (by simp)
  t_fac i j k := (hf j).rep.hom_ext' (by simp) (by simp)
  cocycle i j k := pullback₃.hom_ext (by simp) (by simp) (by simp)
  f_open i j := (hf j).property _ _ _ ((hf i).1.isPullback' (f j)).flip

/-- The map from `X i` to the glued scheme `(glueData hf).glued` -/
noncomputable def toGlued (i : ι) : X i ⟶ (glueData hf).glued :=
  (glueData hf).ι i

instance : IsOpenImmersion (toGlued hf i) :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsOpenImmersion ((glueData hf).ι i))

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- The map from the glued scheme `(glueData hf).glued`, treated as a sheaf, to `F`. -/
noncomputable def yonedaGluedToSheaf :
    zariskiTopology.yoneda.obj (glueData hf).glued ⟶ F where
  -- The map is obtained by finding an object of `F((glueData hf).glued)`.
  hom := yonedaEquiv.symm
  -- This section is obtained from gluing the section corresponding to `f i : Hom(-, X i) ⟶ F`.
    ((glueData hf).sheafValGluedMk (fun i ↦ yonedaEquiv (f i)) (by
      intro i j
      apply yonedaEquiv.symm.injective
      dsimp only [glueData_V, glueData_J, glueData_U, glueData_f, glueData_t]
      rw [yonedaEquiv_naturality, Equiv.symm_apply_apply,
        Functor.map_comp_apply, yonedaEquiv_naturality, yonedaEquiv_naturality,
        Equiv.symm_apply_apply, ← Functor.map_comp_assoc,
        Functor.relativelyRepresentable.symmetry_fst, ((hf i).rep.isPullback' (f j)).w]))

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma yoneda_toGlued_yonedaGluedToSheaf (i : ι) :
    yoneda.map (toGlued hf i) ≫ (yonedaGluedToSheaf hf).hom = f i := by
  apply yonedaEquiv.injective
  rw [yonedaGluedToSheaf, yonedaEquiv_apply, yonedaEquiv_apply,
    NatTrans.comp_app_apply, yoneda_map_app]
  simpa using! GlueData.sheafValGluedMk_val _ _ _ _

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
@[simp]
lemma yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued {i : ι} :

10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60

62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)

79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst

122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg

125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))

131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i

136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp

144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

284	/-- **THE PROJECT'S CENTRAL OPEN OBLIGATION — expected to stay open.**
285	
286	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch`: for a smooth proper geometrically
287	integral curve `C` over an *arbitrary* field `k`, the **étale-sheafified**
288	relative Picard functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` (`PicScheme.picEt`,
289	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`) is representable by a `k`-scheme that is separated
290	and locally of finite type — a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
291	`k`-subschemes. All three conjuncts are parts of that one theorem, which is
292	why they are bundled.
293	
294	**There is no hypothesis on `C(k)`, and that is the point.** This statement is
295	the one the challenge asks for: `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` binds
296	`Jacobian C` for a curve with no rational point, so a representability input
297	carrying `[HasRationalPoint C]` answers a different question. The conditional
298	form survives beside this one as `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` below, clearly
299	labelled as strictly weaker.
300	
301	**Why sheafifying is what makes an unconditional statement possible.** The
302	unsheafified functor `picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is *not*
303	representable over a general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
304	L1292–L1302), and a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical
305	topology. So an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` would be a
306	FALSE statement, not merely an unproved one. Against `picEt` it is Kleiman's own
307	theorem. `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` records the sheaf property that makes
308	the difference, and it is proved rather than assumed.
309	
310	**Expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.**
311	Discharging it means formalising the Kleiman §4 existence proof: the Abel-map
312	slice `Div^d_{C/k} → Pic^d_{C/k}` is a smooth proper equivalence relation whose
313	quotient is a scheme (`smoothProperQuotient`, itself gated on
314	`HasSmoothProperQuotient` because Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity
315	vocabulary), together with `Div` representability (Kleiman §3 Thm `th:repDiv`,
316	which needs the Quot scheme). Neither input is available; the project reaches
317	this statement rather than proving it, and it is the single named `sorry` that
318	the whole Jacobian headline rests on. Do not replace it with a weaker
319	conditional statement to make a count go down.
320	
321	This is the **sole** `sorry` of the seam: everything else below — the
322	representing scheme `PicSchemeEt`, its representability, local finiteness,
323	separatedness and group-scheme structure, the comparison class
324	`PicEtComparisonIso` and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is
325	derived from it.
326	
327	**Why the second conjunct is bundled here rather than given its own `sorry`.**
328	Clause (1) is Kleiman §4; clause (2) is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`): given a
329	section, the comparison `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is an isomorphism. Both are
330	theorems of the same paper and neither is formalised. They are stated as one
331	named obligation on purpose: the `picSharp`-shaped consumer interface
332	(`HasPicScheme`, and through it the tangent-space chain and the `k̄` Albanese
333	witness) needs clause (2) to exist at all, and splitting it out would report the
334	Jacobian headline as resting on *six* open obligations where the mathematics has
335	five. The bundling adds no strength — clause (2) is conditional on a section, so
336	it says nothing about a pointless curve — and it keeps the frontier count honest
337	in both directions. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measures the result rather
338	than asserting it. -/

155	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
156	
157	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
158	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
159	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
160	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
161	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
162	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
163	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
164	
165	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
166	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
167	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
168	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
169	  (etaleSheaf C).property
170

172	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
173	
174	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
175	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
176	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
177	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/

179	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
180	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
181	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
182	
183	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
184	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
185	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
186	
187	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
188	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the

191	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

193	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :

373	representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
374	
375	This is the honest `Pic_{C/k}` of the project — available for every smooth
376	proper geometrically integral curve, with no hypothesis on `C(k)`. The legacy
377	`PicScheme` (representing the unsheafified `picSharp`) exists only under a
378	rational point and is retained for the consumers written against it. -/
379	noncomputable def PicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
380	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
381	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
382	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
383	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
384	  (HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et (C := C)).choose
385	
386	/-- **Representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` by `Pic_{C/k}`, over an arbitrary
387	field**: the natural bijection `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)`.
388	
389	The étale-formulation replacement for `PicScheme.representable`. Consumers of
390	the tangent-space chain should compose with *this* `homEquiv`; the `picSharp`
391	version is available only under `[HasRationalPoint C]`. -/
392	noncomputable def representableEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
393	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
394	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
395	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
396	    (PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy (PicSchemeEt C) :=
397	  Classical.choice (HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et (C := C)).choose_spec.1
398	
399	/-- `Pic_{C/k}` is locally of finite type over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1)),
400	extracted from the étale existence package. Unconditional. -/
401	instance instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
402	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
403	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
404	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
405	    LocallyOfFiniteType (PicSchemeEt C).hom :=
406	  (HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et (C := C)).choose_spec.2.1
407	
408	/-- `Pic_{C/k}` is separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`), extracted from
409	the étale existence package. Unconditional. -/
410	instance instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated {k : Type u} [Field k]
411	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
412	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
413	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
414	    IsSeparated (PicSchemeEt C).hom :=
415	  (HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et (C := C)).choose_spec.2.2
416	
417	/-- The multiplicative avatar of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor,
418	to feed the (multiplicative) `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` API. -/
419	noncomputable def picEtCommGrp {k : Type u} [Field k]
420	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
421	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
422	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
423	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.toCommGrp
424	
425	/-- The set-valued shadows of `picEtCommGrp` and `picEt` agree up to the
426	carrier-preserving `Multiplicative.ofAdd` bijection. -/
427	noncomputable def picEtCommGrpForgetIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
428	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
429	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
430	    PicScheme.picEt C ≅ picEtCommGrp C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
431	  NatIso.ofComponents
432	    (fun T => Equiv.toIso (Multiplicative.ofAdd
433	      (α := (((PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj).obj T : Type (u+1)))))
434	    (fun _ => rfl)
435	
436	/-- **`Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, over an arbitrary base
437	field.** Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
438	structure of the étale Picard sheaf along `representableEt`.
439	
440	The group structure survives sheafification because `PicSharp.etaleSheaf` is
441	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued by construction, so this needs no rational point — in
442	contrast with `groupSchemeStructure`, its `picSharp` counterpart. -/
443	noncomputable instance groupSchemeStructureEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
444	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
445	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
446	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
447	    CommGrpObj (PicSchemeEt C) :=
448	  CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (PicSchemeEt C) (picEtCommGrp C)
449	    ((representableEt C).ofIso (picEtCommGrpForgetIso C))
450	
451	/-- **The comparison that transports representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` to the
452	`picSharp`-shaped consumer interface**, and the one place where the étale
453	formulation costs something.
454	
455	`HasPicScheme` is stated against `picSharp C` because that is the shape every
456	downstream consumer uses — the tangent-space chain of
457	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` composes with `representable`'s `homEquiv` to
458	turn scheme points into line-bundle classes. The obligation above is about
459	`picEt C`. Bridging them is exactly the assertion that the sheafification
460	comparison `PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism of functors, which
461	is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`) — TRUE under a section, and FALSE in general
462	without one.
463	
464	This statement is therefore **NOT** part of the étale seam's obligation, and it
465	is deliberately not given a `sorry`-bodied carrier of its own: the seam has
466	exactly one open obligation (`fgaPicardRepresentability`), and adding a second
467	would misreport the frontier. What is recorded here instead is the *shape* of
468	the bridge, as a hypothesis class that a consumer must supply explicitly at the
469	use site — the same discipline `HasSmoothProperQuotient` follows for Kleiman's
470	quotient lemma, and for the same reason: the statement is true under a section
471	and false without one, so it belongs at the use site rather than in a global
472	instance.
473	
474	The consequence for the headline, stated plainly because it is the shape of the
475	remaining work: over an arbitrary field the project reaches representability of
476	the *étale* functor (`representableEt`), and a consumer wanting the `picSharp`
477	shape must either supply this class or be restated against `picEt`. That
478	restatement is downstream work in `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` (a lane this
479	file does not own), not a defect here. -/
480	theorem picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint {k : Type u} [Field k]
481	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
